content.user_title: Draft AI Literacy Policies and Training Plans
content.value_statement: Organizations need structured records of AI tools, usage rules, and staff training. This guide helps Claude or Codex draft connected AI literacy documents for review.
actual_capabilities: Guide drafting of AI system inventories with provisional prohibited, high-risk, transparency, and minimal-risk triage.
Draft internal AI policies covering acceptable use, data privacy, and approval flows.
Outline separate training tracks for management, general staff, and technical teams.
Draft attendance templates, human oversight logs, and documentation review cycles.
Structure high-risk system review questions around Annex III references.
limitations: The folder contains a Markdown guide, not the original scripts, extension source, or reusable template files.
Outputs are drafts and do not provide official EU certification or guarantee regulatory compliance.
Claims about Digital Omnibus changes and current legal timelines need independent verification; no automatic update mechanism is included.
Risk classifications depend on deployment context, and local labor or works council requirements need qualified legal review.

use_cases.title: Prepare an agency AI register
use_cases.description: Draft a tool inventory, client-data policy, and staff training plan for an agency using generative AI.

use_cases.title: Organize client compliance drafts
use_cases.description: Create coordinated inventory, policy, and training drafts with assumptions and unresolved legal questions for client review.

use_cases.title: Plan technical oversight records
use_cases.description: Outline technical training and human oversight logs for deployments that require further high-risk assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Start an AI inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: We are a 50-person marketing agency using ChatGPT and Midjourney. Draft an AI inventory and list missing deployment details before suggesting provisional risk categories.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: document known tools and unanswered questions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an internal usage policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use our approved inventory: [inventory]. Draft acceptable-use rules, client-data restrictions, and approval flows. Mark assumptions and decisions needing management approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: translate an inventory into policy rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build role-based training tracks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this inventory and policy: [documents]. Draft management, general staff, and technical training tracks. Include attendance records, oversight responsibilities, and review cycles.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect staff responsibilities with training.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble a review-ready documentation pack
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these organizational details: [context]. Assemble inventory, policy, training, attendance, and oversight drafts. Explain provisional triage and flag Annex III questions for counsel. Identify legal timeline claims requiring verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate documents for legal and governance review.

output_examples.input: Draft an inventory and training outline for a marketing agency using ChatGPT and Midjourney.
output: Inventory draft: ChatGPT for copywriting; Midjourney for campaign concepts. Record owners, data inputs, and publication workflows.
Provisional triage: confirm deployment details before assigning risk categories.
Training outline: management oversight, staff privacy and hallucination awareness, and technical approval responsibilities.
Policy draft: do not enter client personal data into unapproved AI tools.

output_examples.input: Prepare attendance and oversight records for our internal AI literacy program.
output: Attendance record: participant, role, training track, session date, and completion status.
Oversight log: system, reviewer, review date, identified issue, decision, and follow-up owner.
Review cycle: assign a policy owner and record the next inventory and training review dates.

best_practices: Provide tool purposes, data categories, deployment contexts, and accountable owners before requesting provisional risk triage.
Keep inventory entries, policy restrictions, and role-based training requirements consistent across generated documents.
Have qualified counsel verify legal references, implementation timelines, and local consultation requirements before adopting drafts.
anti_patterns: Treating generated documents as official certification or proof that all legal obligations are satisfied.
Assigning risk categories solely from product names without examining how each system is deployed.
Assuming the public guide includes executable automation, original templates, or guaranteed regulatory updates.

faq.question: What does this skill help produce?
faq.answer: It guides drafting of AI inventories, usage policies, role-based training plans, attendance templates, oversight logs, and review cycles.

faq.question: Does it certify EU AI Act compliance?
faq.answer: No. It produces draft documentation, not official certification. Qualified counsel should review applicability and legal requirements.

faq.question: Does this folder include scripts or template files?
faq.answer: No. It contains the public Markdown guide. Original scripts, extension source, and templates are explicitly excluded.

faq.question: Which assistants can use the guide?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use its Markdown guidance to draft documents. The guide does not include a separate application.

faq.question: Are legal references updated automatically?
faq.answer: No automatic update mechanism is included. Verify current legislation and timelines independently, including the guide's Digital Omnibus claims.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide organizational roles, AI tools, purposes, data categories, approval processes, and existing training. Omit unnecessary personal or confidential information.
